## Findings

Across the hotrod services, only **redis-manual** has error-status spans in the last 24 hours (frontend, customer, driver, route, and mysql all returned zero error traces for their own spans).

**Origin of the error:**
- **Service:** `redis-manual`
- **Operation (span):** `GetDriver`

Tracing the call chain for one representative error trace (`89e52103a97fd980c331260a8a0da4be`):

```
frontend  /dispatch
  └─ frontend  driver.DriverService/FindNearest (client)   — status OK
       └─ driver  driver.DriverService/FindNearest (server) — status OK
            └─ redis-manual  GetDriver × 10 (parallel lookups)
                 ├─ 8 succeed
                 └─ 2 fail: otel.status_code=ERROR, error=true, "An error occurred"
```

The failing `GetDriver` spans are leaves (no child spans) — this is where the fault actually happens. Notably, the parent spans (`driver.DriverService/FindNearest` and `/dispatch`) both report success (`rpc.grpc.status_code=0`, `http.response.status_code=200`): the driver service retries/tolerates the redis failures and the request succeeds overall, so the error never surfaces at the outer spans. It's only visible by walking down into `redis-manual`'s `GetDriver` spans.

This same pattern (error confined to `redis-manual`/`GetDriver` leaf spans, parents clean) held consistently across all 20 sampled error traces for `redis-manual`.

**Note:** I hit the session's tool-approval flow repeatedly on `python3`/multi-op Bash commands (each required manual approval), and the budget is now nearly exhausted (~$0.05 left), so I did not exhaustively re-verify every one of the 20 traces span-by-span — I relied on the aggregate error-tag scan (all 96 error-tagged spans were `GetDriver`/`redis-manual`) plus one fully-expanded trace to confirm the leaf/parent relationship.
